papers.title: Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
papers.summary: Post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial (994 patients with STEMI and multivessel disease randomised to immediate or in-hospital staged FFR-guided complete revascularisation). Age modified the treatment effect on 1-year death, MI or unplanned revascularisation (interaction P=0.015), with risk rising in the immediate arm beyond about 67 years. In patients aged 70 or over, immediate complete revascularisation had more events than staged, 22.3% versus 13.8% (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.06-2.69); under 70 there was no difference, 6.8% versus 8.4% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.45-1.45).
papers.study_type: Post hoc analysis of a randomised trial
papers.short_title: Immediate versus staged complete revascularisation by age in STEMI: OPTION-STEMI

papers.title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of randomised trials on coronary artery disease management in patients undergoing TAVI: five trials (1,644 patients), four in the main synthesis (1,476). Routine PCI versus conservative treatment lowered MACE (RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI 0.11-0.83) but increased major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI reduced MACE, stroke and unplanned revascularisation versus conservative treatment and ranked highest for ischaemic outcomes.
papers.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
papers.short_title: Coronary disease management in TAVI patients: meta-analysis

papers.title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
papers.summary: Single-arm pivotal trial of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (RV/LV ratio above 0.9, haemodynamically stable) at 19 US and European sites. In 123 patients, 48-hour major adverse events occurred in 2.4% (3 of 123), and the RV/LV ratio fell from 1.44 to 1.05 at 48 hours (mean reduction 0.39); both met their prespecified performance goals (P<0.0001).
papers.short_title: Vertex aspiration thrombectomy for intermediate-risk PE: SPIRARE II

papers.title: Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch.
papers.summary: Series of 62 consecutive patients from 6 US and Canadian centres undergoing transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction from the left heart or aortic arch. Feasibility was 85.5% and effectiveness (at least 70% debulking) 77.4%; in 8.1% no mass was found during the procedure. The 30-day VARC-3 safety endpoint occurred in 14.5%, including 3.2% procedure-attributable mortality and 6.5% stroke, which the authors say calls for better case selection and embolic protection.
papers.short_title: Vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and aortic arch

papers.title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
papers.summary: Cohort of 12,847 adults aged 30 to 45 from the CAC Consortium, followed for a median 22.6 years. Compared with a CAC score of 0, a CAC score greater than 90% carried adjusted hazard ratios of 1.87 for all-cause, 2.60 for cardiovascular and 3.71 for coronary heart disease mortality.
papers.short_title: coronary calcium in young adults and 30-year mortality

papers.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of 85 randomised trials (70,543 participants) with cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure or chronic kidney disease. Versus control, SGLT2 inhibitors raised haemoglobin by 0.60 g/dL and haematocrit by 2.36 percentage points, increased erythropoietin and lowered transferrin saturation. The authors say the clinical significance of these small increases is unclear.
papers.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs

papers.title: Life expectancy after aortic valve replacement: a nationwide analysis.
papers.summary: No abstract was available for this study, so no results are reported here. Judging from its title, it is a nationwide analysis of life expectancy in patients after aortic valve replacement. See the full paper in EuroIntervention for the study population, methods and main findings.
papers.short_title: life expectancy after aortic valve replacement
